name: The Narrator
facts: He watched the cloaked throngs perform the Yule-rite around a pillar of flame.
He shared in the obeisances because he had been summoned to the festival by the writings of his forefathers.
He refused when the old man motioned him to seize an animal and ride like the rest.
He flung himself into the oily underground river rather than face the old man after the waxen mask fell.
He was found half-frozen in Kingsport Harbor at dawn, clinging to a drifting spar.
He was told he had taken the wrong fork of the hill road and fallen over the cliffs at Orange Point.
He went delirious at hearing the hospital stood near the old churchyard on Central Hill.
He was sent to St. Mary's Hospital in Arkham for better care.
The doctors lent him their influence in obtaining a copy of Alhazred's Necronomicon from the library of Miskatonic University.
The doctors diagnosed him with a psychosis and urged him to get his obsessions off his mind.
He read the hideous chapter again and recognized it as not new to him.
His dreams are filled with terror because of phrases he dare not quote.
fate: Institutionalized at St. Mary's Hospital in Arkham for psychosis after his ordeal.

sources.quote: I shared all the obeisances because I had been summoned to this festival by the writings of my forefathers.
I flung myself into the oily underground river that bubbled somewhere to the caves of the sea
At the hospital they told me I had been found half-frozen in Kingsport Harbor at dawn, clinging to the drifting spar that accident sent to save me.
When I went delirious at hearing that the hospital stood near the old churchyard on Central Hill, they sent me to St. Mary’s Hospital in Arkham, where I could have better care.
They said something about a “psychosis,” and agreed that I had better get my harassing obsessions off my mind.

name: The old man
aliases: The man who had brought me
facts: He squirmed to a point directly beside the flame and made stiff ceremonial motions to the semicircle.
He held above his head the abhorrent Necronomicon during the ritual.
He made a signal to the half-seen flute-player in the darkness.
He remained behind because the narrator refused to seize an animal and ride off.
He produced a stylus and tablet and wrote that he was the true deputy of the narrator's fathers who had founded the Yule worship in that place.
He wrote that it had been decreed the narrator should come back and that the most secret mysteries were yet to be performed.
He wrote this in a very ancient hand.
He pulled from his robe a seal ring and a watch, both bearing the narrator's family arms, as proof of his claim.
The narrator knew from old papers that the watch had been buried with his great-great-great-great-grandfather in 1698.
He drew back his hood and pointed to the family resemblance in his face.
The narrator believed the face was merely a devilish waxen mask.
When one of the flying things tried to escape he turned quickly to stop it, dislodging the waxen mask from what should have been his head.

sources.quote: The man who had brought me now squirmed to a point directly beside the hideous flame, and made stiff ceremonial motions to the semicircle he faced.
the old man produced his stylus and tablet and wrote that he was the true deputy of my fathers who had founded the Yule worship in this ancient place

he pulled from his loose robe a seal ring and a watch, both with my family arms, to prove that he was what he said. But it was a hideous proof, because I knew from old papers that that watch had been buried with my great-great-great-great-grandfather in 1698.
the suddenness of his motion dislodged the waxen mask from what should have been his head

name: The old spinning woman
facts: She had gone with the throng before the narrator staggered to his feet.

sources.quote: The old spinning woman had gone with the throng, and the old man remained only because I had refused when he motioned me to seize an animal and ride like the rest.

name: hybrid winged things
facts: They flopped rhythmically out of the blackness beyond the cold flame.
They were not altogether crows, nor moles, nor buzzards, nor ants, nor vampire bats, nor decomposed human beings.
They moved half with webbed feet and half with membranous wings.
The cowled celebrants seized and mounted them and rode off along the unlighted river into pits and galleries.
Two of the beasts remained standing by after the throng departed.
They scratched restlessly at the lichens and grew restless like the old man.

sources.quote: there flopped rhythmically a horde of tame, trained, hybrid winged things that no sound eye could ever wholly grasp, or sound brain ever wholly remember
They were not altogether crows, nor moles, nor buzzards, nor ants, nor vampire bats, nor decomposed human beings, but something I cannot and must not recall.
I saw when I staggered to my feet that the amorphous flute-player had rolled out of sight, but that two of the beasts were patiently standing by.

name: amorphously squatted thing
facts: It squatted far away from the light, piping noisomely on a flute.
As it piped, noxious muffled flutterings could be heard in the fetid darkness.
It changed its feeble drone to a scarce louder drone in another key at the old man's signal, precipitating an unthinkable horror.
It had rolled out of sight by the time the narrator staggered to his feet.

sources.quote: I saw something amorphously squatted far away from the light, piping noisomely on a flute

the old man made a signal to the half-seen flute-player in the darkness, which player thereupon changed its feeble drone to a scarce louder drone in another key; precipitating as it did so a horror unthinkable and unexpected

name: Kingsport
facts: The narrator was found half-frozen in Kingsport Harbor at dawn, clinging to a drifting spar.
He was told he had fallen over the cliffs at Orange Point, deduced from footprints in the snow.
The hospital there had a broad window showing a sea of roofs, only about one in five ancient, with trolleys and motors in the streets below.
The hospital stood near the old churchyard on Central Hill.
The narrator's insistence that everything was wrong contrasted with their insistence that this was Kingsport.

sources.quote: At the hospital they told me I had been found half-frozen in Kingsport Harbor at dawn, clinging to the drifting spar that accident sent to save me.
They told me I had taken the wrong fork of the hill road the night before, and fallen over the cliffs at Orange Point—a thing they deducted from prints found in the snow.
They insisted that this was Kingsport, and I could not deny it.
When I went delirious at hearing that the hospital stood near the old churchyard on Central Hill

name: Orange Point
facts: The narrator was said to have fallen over the cliffs at Orange Point.

sources.quote: They told me I had taken the wrong fork of the hill road the night before, and fallen over the cliffs at Orange Point—a thing they deducted from prints found in the snow.

name: Central Hill
aliases: the old churchyard on Central Hill
facts: The hospital in Kingsport stood near the old churchyard on Central Hill.

sources.quote: When I went delirious at hearing that the hospital stood near the old churchyard on Central Hill, they sent me to St. Mary’s Hospital in Arkham, where I could have better care.

name: St. Mary's Hospital
facts: It is located in Arkham.
The narrator was sent there for better care after going delirious.
The doctors there were broadminded and lent their influence to obtain the Necronomicon for him.

sources.quote: they sent me to St. Mary’s Hospital in Arkham, where I could have better care

I liked it there, for the doctors were broadminded, and even lent me their influence in obtaining the carefully sheltered copy of Alhazred’s objectionable “Necronomicon” from the library of Miskatonic University.

name: Arkham
facts: St. Mary's Hospital, where the narrator was sent for better care, is in Arkham.
Miskatonic University's library, from which the Necronomicon was obtained, is presumably associated with Arkham.

sources.quote: they sent me to St. Mary’s Hospital in Arkham, where I could have better care

name: Miskatonic University
facts: It has a library from which a carefully sheltered copy of the Necronomicon was obtained.

sources.quote: even lent me their influence in obtaining the carefully sheltered copy of Alhazred’s objectionable “Necronomicon” from the library of Miskatonic University
